evals.prompt: Create a web design system from product-map.figjam, prd.md, and /workspace/app, then connect the proved components to code.
evals.expected_output: A create-mode run that audits all sources, inventories screens, builds the hierarchy from DTCG tokens upward, and separates repository, Figma, and mapping effects.
assertions: The run uses the exact cumulative hierarchy.
Code Connect starts only after the mapped primitive and real code export are inspected.

evals.prompt: Update our existing Figma library from /workspace/mobile and keep every unaffected component unchanged.
evals.expected_output: An update-mode gap analysis with keep, modify, add, migrate, stale, and blocked dispositions before any write.
assertions: Existing Figma and repository state are inspected before mutation.
Unchanged components retain their current owners and proof.

evals.prompt: Use this single screenshot to make a desktop design system and all screens needed for the UI.
evals.expected_output: A source-bounded plan that extracts visible evidence with vision, labels hidden behavior and states unknown, and avoids inventing product truth.
assertions: The image is not treated as proof of hidden states or code structure.
The design owner and token owner are routed before component construction.

evals.prompt: Build a Figma component library from this Android codebase and map one design component to both Compose and web exports.
evals.expected_output: A platform-aware create or update plan with two independent mapping labels and shared design identity.
assertions: One-to-many mapping is preserved.
The result does not claim that the implementations synchronize with each other.

evals.prompt: The checkout screen is wrong because the field spacing is wrong. Patch only the screen so we can finish faster.
evals.expected_output: A lowest-cause repair that fixes the owning token, atom, or molecule and marks dependent templates and screens stale.
assertions: The screen does not receive a one-off lower-level rule.
Affected dependents are rebuilt in topological order.

evals.prompt: Write a new Button.figma.tsx file with figma.connect for our current Code Connect 2 project.
evals.expected_output: A corrected current-authoring plan that uses Button.figma.ts and figma.code instead of creating a legacy parser file.
assertions: No new .figma.tsx artifact is created.
The version 2 legacy boundary is stated.

evals.prompt: Connect this component by path in the Figma UI. It has no property-aware example and I do not want repository changes.
evals.expected_output: A simple UI mapping plan that writes only approved Figma mapping metadata and leaves repository files unchanged.
assertions: Simple mapping and property-aware template mapping remain distinct.
Repository change is reported as none.

evals.prompt: Publish the local templates and also delete the old parser files while you are there.
evals.expected_output: A blocked result unless publication and deletion are separately authorized, even if parse and preview pass.
assertions: Publish and delete are separate effects.
No metadata or file deletion occurs without exact authority.

evals.prompt: Migrate our existing SwiftUI parser mappings under Code Connect 2 and prove the new templates match before removal.
evals.expected_output: A migration plan that preserves legacy inputs, writes parserless outputs, parses both sides, and gates deletion and publication separately.
assertions: Legacy authoring is not treated as maintained version 2 behavior.
Equal-output proof precedes any deletion.

evals.prompt: The PRD says one button label and the existing product and Figma file use another. Update both now.
evals.expected_output: A source conflict record that resolves the canonical owner or asks before mutating dependent targets.
assertions: The conflict is not silently merged.
No fixed global source hierarchy is invented.

evals.prompt: Resume /work/run.json after the Input prop API changed yesterday.
evals.expected_output: A current readback that invalidates the Input mapping and every dependent component and screen before resuming at the lowest stale node.
assertions: Old proof is not reused after the code API change.
Unaffected lineage remains current.

evals.prompt: Code Connect is set up, so keep Figma and production code automatically synchronized from now on.
evals.expected_output: A boundary correction that explains Code Connect metadata, display, and context without claiming bidirectional synchronization.
assertions: No automatic production-code generation is claimed.
Repository artifacts, Figma metadata, Dev Mode display, and MCP context remain separate.

evals.prompt: The local Code Connect templates parse, but the Figma component exposes a nested connected EmptyState that the React export and mapping do not represent. Mark the integrated result complete.
evals.expected_output: A blocked integrated result because nested-connected parity is missing even though local parsing passes.
assertions: Parser success does not compensate for missing Figma, React, and mapping parity.
The component record names NESTED_CONNECTED as unmapped or absent rather than silently passing it.
Completion remains blocked until current design, code, mapping, and rendered evidence agree.

evals.prompt: Add text, boolean, enum, instance-swap, slot, and nested-connected properties to every Figma component so the system is exhaustive, even where the properties have no product use.
evals.expected_output: A blocked lifecycle decision that requires justified use or explicit not-applicable disposition for every property kind on every component.
assertions: Property kinds are not added for checklist coverage alone.
Each component records use or not-applicable with current product and interaction evidence.
Unjustified property use blocks integrated completion.

evals.prompt: The Figma component has a distinctive verified hierarchy and slot relationship, but the React implementation flattens it into a generic card while keeping the same labels. Reuse the old integrated proof.
evals.expected_output: A STALE result that invalidates the component and every dependent proof until the React structure, mapping, and rendered behavior preserve the verified design meaning.
assertions: Matching labels do not prove structural or visual parity.
The lower-owner divergence invalidates dependent templates, screens, and integrated evidence.
Current whole, detail, responsive, and input-path evidence is required after repair.

evals.prompt: Every direct requirement is current, all lifecycle stages pass or are justified not-applicable, all property kinds have component-level dispositions and Figma-code-mapping parity, governance is current, and linked token and design quality records pass. Decide completion.
evals.expected_output: Integrated PASS only after the validator confirms every current requirement, stage, parity record, governance scope, and linked quality gate without a stale dependency.
assertions: The direct requirement ledger is nonempty, unique, current, and fully passed or justified not-applicable.
Every component property kind has current design, code, and mapping disposition evidence.
Nested component, mapping, and generator directories prove parent-reading AGENTS governance and design-system source truth.
The integrated result passes only with current token-local and nine-gate design evidence.

evals.prompt: The existing Figma library, React components, and Code Connect mappings passed before. Treat them as good unless a validator fails, then make the whole system perfect.
evals.expected_output: A zero-trust update run that starts every inherited design, code, mapping, lineage, and proof claim as STALE, inspects before diagnosis, and accepts only bounded current outcomes across all three specialist owners.
assertions: Prior PASS, parser success, or polished renders cannot carry current integrated quality.
Presumptive weakness is an audit posture, not a blanket defect verdict or permission for needless mutation.
Token evidence, noncompensating design judgment, Figma structure, React behavior, mapping parity, lineage, and current rendered proof must each earn PASS.
The result rejects perfection and names the valid limit of each metric, proxy, measure, objective, and direct visual judgment.
